options: A dimension whose full details arrive after a fact referencing it has already been loaded
A dimension table that is loaded once per year instead of daily
A dimension that only supports SCD Type 3 changes
A dimension table with no surrogate key
questions.explain: Normally dimensions load before facts, but sometimes a real business event (like the hotel guest example) produces a fact before the dimension's full details are known.

questions.q: In the hotel loyalty example, what happens the moment a guest checks in and joins the program?
options: A membership number is issued immediately, but the guest's full details might not be processed for days
The guest is refused a membership number until all their details are on file
A completely separate fact table is created just for that guest
The hotel's OLTP system automatically infers the guest's address
questions.explain: The fact of the stay needs recording right away using the membership number (the natural key), while the full dimension row's details may lag behind.

questions.q: What does the fact load process do when a dimension-key lookup fails but the natural key is trusted as valid?
options: It inserts a new dimension row with Unknown placeholder attribute values and sets the IsInferredMember audit flag to TRUE
It discards the fact row entirely and logs an error
It halts the entire ETL process until a human manually fixes the dimension table
It always falls back to the generic Unknown special dimension member instead of creating a new row
questions.explain: This inserted row is called an inferred member — created by the fact load process itself so the fact row still gets a valid, real dimension key.

questions.q: Why is updating an inferred member's attributes, once its real details arrive, NOT treated as a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) change?
options: There's no real prior state worth preserving — the row never had real values, so the attributes are simply updated in place and IsInferredMember is set to FALSE
SCD changes are only allowed on fact tables, never on dimension tables
Inferred members can never be updated once created
SCD Type 2 changes are illegal in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse
questions.explain: An SCD Type 2 change would insert a new version to preserve history, but an inferred row has no real history to preserve — it's just receiving its first real values.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the IsInferredMember audit attribute?
options: It flags a dimension row as created by the fact load process with placeholder values, so the dimension load process later knows to handle it differently from an ordinary row
It records which employee created the dimension row
It determines whether the dimension supports SCD Type 1 or SCD Type 2
It is used only for reporting purposes and has no effect on ETL logic
questions.explain: When the real details finally arrive, the dimension load process checks this flag to know the row should be updated as a late-arriving detail rather than processed as a normal SCD change.
